legal_name.notes: The fuller form Ricardo Leyva Muñoz Ramírez circulates widely. The appellate opinion uses 'Richard Ramirez'; the longer form has not been confirmed against a record and is not asserted.

media_epithet.notes: Press epithet assigned during the offending period. Analytically consequential here in a way it is nowhere else in the dataset: the coverage that attached this label is the same coverage that published his photograph, which is what led directly to his capture. Note the collision with USA-004-DEANGELO, who also carried 'Original Night Stalker' — evidence that press epithets are not identifiers and must never be used as keys.

birth_date.notes: Commonly given as 29 February 1960, and a leap-day birth is the kind of detail that would be trivial to confirm from a Texas birth record or the trial file. Neither has been retrieved, and every accessible secondary source located was a wiki or aggregator. The contemporaneous death report gives his age as 53 on 7 June 2013, which constrains the birth to between June 1959 and June 1960 — consistent with, but not proof of, the circulating date. [SEARCH NOT EXHAUSTED — a research todo, not a finding.]

birth_place.notes: Commonly given as El Paso, Texas. No record retrieved. [SEARCH NOT EXHAUSTED — a research todo, not a finding.]

death_date.notes: Died at Marin General Hospital, aged 53, while under sentence of death at San Quentin. The Marin County Coroner determined the cause as complications of B-cell lymphoma, with chronic substance abuse and hepatitis C viral infection as contributing conditions.

judicial_status.value: Deceased. Convicted of 13 counts of murder and numerous sexual and burglary offences; sentenced to death and died in custody before execution.

convictions.notes: The homicide counts are 12 first-degree plus 1 second-degree, totalling 13. Sources that give '13 counts of first-degree murder' are wrong on the composition even where the total is right. The burglary counts matter analytically: this offender was convicted of more burglaries than homicides, and the offence structure was residential intrusion first.

NPR. "'Night Stalker' Richard Ramirez Dies In Prison." 7 June 2013.

confirmed_victim_count.notes: Homicide convictions only. Five surviving victims of attempted murder, and the victims of the sexual and burglary counts, are not included in this figure and are not enumerated here.

sources.citation: CBS News. 'DNA Links "Night Stalker" Richard Ramirez to 1984 Killing of 9-Year-Old Mei Leung.' 23 October 2009.

attributed_victim_count.notes: One further homicide attributed by a named agency and never charged: the San Francisco Police Department announced on 23 October 2009 that a CODIS cold hit linked him to the April 1984 killing of Mei Leung, aged nine, in San Francisco. He was already under sentence of death and no charge followed. The attribution is agency-sourced, which is why it is recorded — but it is 'reported', not 'established': the announcement described a database hit for which a confirmatory sample was still being obtained, and this dataset has not retrieved the confirmation. Later San Francisco reporting is understood to have complicated the picture; see data_quality.contested_points.

claimed_victim_count.notes: No stable self-reported total has been retrieved. He contested the charges through trial and appeal rather than claiming offences.

estimate_provenance.value: The homicide count derives from the conviction record; the single additional attribution derives from a police announcement of a database match. No press-synthesised higher figure is recorded.

People v. Ramirez, 39 Cal. 4th 398, 139 P.3d 64 (Cal. 2006)

first_known_offence.notes: The killing of Jennie Vincow, the offence whose crime scene produced the fingerprint evidence that later identified him. Note that the SFPD attribution places an uncharged homicide two months earlier, in April 1984.

sources.citation: People v. Ramirez, 39 Cal. 4th 398, 139 P.3d 64 (Cal. 2006)

last_known_offence.notes: Apprehended 31 August 1985. The charged series therefore spans roughly fourteen months — by a wide margin the shortest offending period in this dataset.

jurisdictions.notes: The charged offences occurred across Los Angeles, Rosemead, Monterey Park, Monrovia, Burbank and Arcadia — a wide spread within one county.

employment_history.notes: No record retrieved. Note the contrast with DeAngelo, Ridgway, Rader and Gacy, where a stable occupation was structurally load-bearing. Here there appears to have been none — but that is an impression from absence, not a finding, until someone checks. [SEARCH NOT EXHAUSTED — a research todo, not a finding.]

documented_head_injury.notes: Childhood head injuries are asserted in secondary literature and were advanced in mitigation. No medical documentation has been located, and medical records of this kind are not public. Recorded as an established absence for that reason, not because the claim is implausible.

formal_diagnoses.notes: No insanity defence was mounted and no court-adopted diagnosis has been located in the appellate record. Compare USA-005-GACY, the only record in this dataset where competing clinical evidence was tested at trial.

psychometric_results.notes: No instrument, administrator or date retrieved.

commentary_attributions.notes: Not catalogued. This subject attracted an unusually large volume of commentary framed around occult symbolism, most of it generated by the trial's media coverage rather than by clinicians.

victim_selection.value: Offences were committed against occupants of private residences entered at night, across a wide spread of suburban communities. Victims spanned a broad range of ages and both sexes. The access condition exploited was residential: unsecured entry points in single-family housing.

sources.citation: People v. Ramirez, 39 Cal. 4th 398, 139 P.3d 64 (Cal. 2006)

victim_selection.notes: Recorded as an access condition, not as a characteristic that explains the deaths. The absence of a narrow victim profile is itself notable: it is part of why the series generated exceptional public fear, and it distinguishes this case from USA-002-RIDGWAY and USA-007-DAHMER, where a specific and institutionally disregarded population was targeted.

sources.citation: People v. Ramirez, 39 Cal. 4th 398, 139 P.3d 64 (Cal. 2006)

approach_method.notes: Fourteen first-degree burglary convictions establish the pattern judicially. Compare USA-004-DEANGELO, whose offence structure was also residential intrusion at night.

sources.citation: Canter, David and Paul Larkin. 'The Environmental Range of Serial Rapists.' Journal of Environmental Psychology 13(1), 1993, 63-69.

spatial_pattern.notes: Coded commuter: offences dispersed across many communities within Los Angeles County, plus an uncharged attribution in San Francisco. Maintainer coding applying the Canter & Larkin framework, not a source-attested fact. The dataset now holds three commuters (Bundy, DeAngelo, Ramirez) and four marauders (Ridgway, Gacy, Rader, Dahmer). Detection delay still does not order by range: this commuter was caught in fourteen months, the marauder Ridgway took nineteen years.

weapon_or_method.notes: The appellate opinion records varied methods across the counts but the summary retrieved does not itemise them reliably. A contributor should populate this from the opinion's statement of facts rather than from press description. [SEARCH NOT EXHAUSTED — a research todo, not a finding.]

signature_behaviour.notes: Occult symbols left at scenes are among the most widely repeated claims about this case and are not entered here: the retrieved sources do not document them, and this dataset does not accept press characterisation for scene conduct. The trial record would settle it either way, which is why this is a todo rather than a finding. [SEARCH NOT EXHAUSTED — a research todo, not a finding.]

forensic_countermeasures.notes: No countermeasure conduct is established. The fingerprint left on a window screen at the first charged homicide is what eventually identified him, which is evidence against any systematic countermeasure practice.

Canter, David V., Laurence J. Alison, Emily Alison and Natalia Wentink. 'The Organized/Disorganized Typology of Serial Murder: Myth or Model?' Psychology, Public Policy, and Law 10(3), 2004, 293-320.

motive_classification.notes: Maintainer coding, not a source-attested fact, and a poor fit. Coded from the sexual offences tried alongside the homicides, but the conviction record contains more burglary counts than homicide counts, which points as much to an instrumental classification. This is a case where the Holmes & Holmes categories do not cleanly apply, and that is worth recording rather than resolving: Canter et al. (2004) is cited precisely because typologies of this family have a weak empirical record. A contributor may reasonably code this differently or decline to code it.

detection_delay_factors.value: Roughly fourteen months elapsed between the first charged homicide in June 1984 and apprehension on 31 August 1985 — the shortest interval in this dataset by a wide margin. The case was not closed by an investigation reaching a conclusion. Fingerprint evidence identified him, his photograph was released to the media on 30 August 1985, and members of the public recognised him in East Los Angeles the following day and physically detained him until police arrived.

sources.citation: People v. Ramirez, 39 Cal. 4th 398, 139 P.3d 64 (Cal. 2006)
NPR. "'Night Stalker' Richard Ramirez Dies In Prison." 7 June 2013.

detection_delay_factors.notes: A SEVENTH DELAY MECHANISM, and the inverse of the others. Bundy: jurisdictional fragmentation. Ridgway: institutional neglect plus forensic limits. DeAngelo: absent technology. Gacy: an unconnected conviction record. Rader: none — he surfaced. Dahmer: present information actively dismissed. Ramirez: the shortest delay in the dataset, ended by publication and public recognition rather than by arrest. Any analysis of investigative effectiveness must count this alongside Rader as a case the investigation did not close by itself — here because the public closed it first.

identifying_evidence.value: Fingerprints recovered from a window screen at the scene of the first charged homicide, later identified as his.

sources.citation: People v. Ramirez, 39 Cal. 4th 398, 139 P.3d 64 (Cal. 2006)

identifying_evidence.notes: The identification is routinely attributed to California's then-new automated fingerprint identification system. The appellate opinion establishes the fingerprint evidence but not the mechanism of the match, and the AFIS attribution is not asserted here — see data_quality.known_gaps.

forensic_methods_used.value: Latent fingerprint comparison at the time of the investigation. DNA profiling was applied decades later: a CODIS database search produced a cold hit linking him to an uncharged 1984 homicide, announced by the San Francisco Police Department in October 2009.

sources.citation: People v. Ramirez, 39 Cal. 4th 398, 139 P.3d 64 (Cal. 2006)
CBS News. 'DNA Links "Night Stalker" Richard Ramirez to 1984 Killing of 9-Year-Old Mei Leung.' 23 October 2009.

forensic_methods_used.notes: The CODIS route is worth distinguishing from the identification pathways in USA-004-DEANGELO and USA-006-RADER. Here the offender was already in a criminal database because he had been convicted; no third party's genetic or medical data was involved. That is the uncontroversial form of forensic DNA use, and recording it alongside the other two makes the contrast visible.

method_now_disputed.notes: No technique relied on in this conviction has been found scientifically unreliable. Latent print comparison has been criticised for overstated certainty claims in expert testimony, but it has not been discredited in the way bite-mark comparison has, and the retrieved record does not show it being overstated here.

arrest.value: Apprehended on 31 August 1985 in East Los Angeles by members of the public, one of whom struck him with a steel bar, after his photograph was released to the media the previous day.

sources.citation: People v. Ramirez, 39 Cal. 4th 398, 139 P.3d 64 (Cal. 2006)
NPR. "'Night Stalker' Richard Ramirez Dies In Prison." 7 June 2013.

arrest.notes: Recorded because it is established by the appellate record, and because it is the only apprehension in this dataset effected by civilians. The individuals involved are not named.

interrogation_method.notes: No interrogation record retrieved. The case rested on physical evidence and identification, not on admissions.

confession_reliability.value: Not load-bearing. He contested the charges through trial and on appeal. Nothing in the victim count depends on anything he said.

confession_reliability.notes: One of only three records in the dataset where no field depends on offender self-report, alongside USA-005-GACY and USA-008 itself. Compare USA-003-HALL, where self-report was the entire case.

trial_outcome.value: Tried in Los Angeles County. Jury verdicts of guilty accepted on 20 September 1989, with special circumstances found true.

NPR. "'Night Stalker' Richard Ramirez Dies In Prison." 7 June 2013.

trial_outcome.notes: The only fully contested jury trial on the homicide counts in this dataset apart from USA-005-GACY. Bundy was tried; Ridgway, DeAngelo and Rader pleaded; Dahmer conceded the acts and litigated only responsibility.

sources.citation: People v. Ramirez, 39 Cal. 4th 398, 139 P.3d 64 (Cal. 2006)
NPR. "'Night Stalker' Richard Ramirez Dies In Prison." 7 June 2013.

appellate_history.value: Automatic direct appeal to the Supreme Court of California; judgment affirmed 7 August 2006, roughly seventeen years after sentence.

sources.citation: People v. Ramirez, 39 Cal. 4th 398, 139 P.3d 64 (Cal. 2006)

appellate_history.notes: The interval between sentence and affirmance is itself a datum about capital procedure in California.

disposition.value: Died in custody on 7 June 2013 at Marin General Hospital, under sentence of death at San Quentin, having spent approximately twenty-three years on death row without execution.

sources.citation: Marin County Coroner, findings on the death of Richard Ramirez, 2013
NPR. "'Night Stalker' Richard Ramirez Dies In Prison." 7 June 2013.

disposition.notes: Sentenced to death and not executed. Bundy and Gacy, both sentenced earlier, were executed; Ramirez outlived his sentence by two decades under California's effective moratorium. The dataset now records three death sentences with three different outcomes, which is a fact about jurisdictions rather than about offenders.

known_gaps: Birth date and place not asserted; every accessible secondary source was inadmissible. A Texas birth record or the trial file would settle it.

The AFIS attribution for the fingerprint match is not established. The appellate opinion records the fingerprint evidence but not how the match was made, and this case is routinely cited as an early automated-identification success — a claim that should be sourced or dropped.
Weapon and method are not itemised per count; the opinion's statement of facts has not been worked through.
Signature behaviour is a todo, not a finding: the widely repeated occult-symbol claims are unsourced here and the trial record would resolve them.
Education, employment and military service all unsearched.
The confirmatory DNA sample sought in 2009 has not been traced, so the San Francisco attribution rests on an unconfirmed database hit.
contested_points: The 2009 San Francisco attribution. The announcement described a CODIS cold hit pending confirmation, no charge ever followed, and later San Francisco reporting is understood to have raised questions including the presence of a second DNA profile. A contributor should retrieve that reporting; until then the attribution stays 'reported' and the caveat stands.
Whether the Holmes & Holmes motive coding applies at all to an offence structure with more burglary counts than homicide counts.
excluded_material: Occult symbolism as an established feature of the offences — extensively asserted, not sourced here.
Graphic description of the offences, excluded under ETHICS.md.

Names of the five surviving attempted-murder victims and of the sexual-offence victims. The one named victim in this record, in the uncharged San Francisco attribution, is named because the police announcement identifying the case does so and no other identifier for it exists.

Childhood aetiologies advanced in mitigation and repeated as established causation.
